bracket: [Textbook answer-key error: the printed answer is 1.274, which is exactly \( 4/\pi \) -- the value obtained by replacing \( \sin 45^\circ \) with \( 45^\circ \) expressed in radians (\( \pi/4 = 0.7854 \)). The small-angle approximation \( \sin\theta \approx \theta \) is not valid at \( 45^\circ \), where it is in error by about 11 %. The printed value is self-refuting: substituting \( a/\lambda = 1.274 \) back into the book's own condition \( a\sin\theta = \lambda \) gives \( \sin\theta = 0.7849 \), i.e. \( \theta = 51.7^\circ \), contradicting the \( 45.0^\circ \) stated in the question itself. The correct answer is \( 1/\sin 45^\circ = \sqrt{2} \approx 1.414 \), which back-solves to exactly \( 45.00^\circ \).]

[Textbook misprint: Table 7.1 on the Comparison page carries two errors in its *Single slit diffraction pattern* column, so the expressions derived here will not match that table. (i) The angular positions are printed as \( \left(n + \tfrac{1}{2}\right)\left(\lambda/d\right) \) and \( n\left(\lambda/d\right) \), using the slit SEPARATION \( d \); they must use the slit WIDTH \( a \), as the legend above that table itself states and as the same column's own fringe-width entry \( W = \lambda D/a \) and distance entries confirm. (ii) The distance of the \( n^{\text{th}} \) bright fringe is printed as \( \left(n + \tfrac{1}{2}\right)\left(\lambda D/a\right) = nW \); since \( W = \lambda D/a \) that expression equals \( \left(n + \tfrac{1}{2}\right)W \), not \( nW \), and the book's own running text states it correctly as \( \left(n + \tfrac{1}{2}\right)W \). Both were verified against the printed page at magnification; the derivation above follows the book's equations and its body text, not the table.]
